articles.title: Luxury real estate brokers and their brother convicted in federal sex trafficking trial
articles.summary: Two high-profile luxury real estate brokers and their other brother were convicted Monday in a sex trafficking trial in which they were accused of using drugs and their influence to sexually abuse women.
articles.body: Two high-profile luxury real estate brokers and their other brother were convicted Monday in a sex trafficking trial in which they were accused of using drugs and their influence to sexually abuse women. Oren, Tal and Alon Alexander were found guilty in federal court in New York City on all 10 counts of engaging in a yearslong conspiracy of rape, sex trafficking, sex abuse and sexual exploitation. A jury of six men and six women delivered the verdict Monday after a monthlong trial that featured testimony from more than 30 witnesses. They began deliberating Thursday. The brothers, whom federal prosecutors in Manhattan charged in December 2024, face up to life in prison. They are set to be sentenced in August. Jay Clayton, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York, thanked the 11 accusers who testified at trial Monday. "These are chilling, reprehensible, and unacceptable acts," he said in a statement, adding, "They bravely overcame the pain of reliving the abuses inflicted upon them and, as a result, prevented others from becoming victims." At trial, prosecutor Madison Smyser said in her opening statement that the three brothers worked together for years “raping women and girls ... with promises of parties and trips, and when they got there the defendants raped them.” The brothers have denied the allegations. Eleven accusers testified. Six of them are part of the indictment against the brothers. One victim, who testified under the pseudonym Katie Moore, said Alon Alexander drugged and raped her after a night out at a New York City club. Moore told the court that after she was handed a drink, her “body started to sway.” “In that moment, it felt sudden. I know I wasn’t drunk or losing control; there was no gradual fade-out. I had never experienced that sort of loss of control of my body before,” she said. Moore said that Alon and Tal Alexander made her and her friend leave the club and that she vaguely remembered getting into a cab. She testified that the thing she remembered was “coming to” and being naked on a bed with Alon Alexander, who did not have any clothes on, standing over her. “I tried to get out of the bed a few times, but Alon kept pushing me back down,” she said. “Finally, he sat down on the bed, and I was able to get up, and I said, ‘I don’t want to have sex with you,’ and he said, ‘You already did.’” One of the charges against Oren Alexander is in connection with an allegation of sexual exploitation of a minor. Prosecutors accused him of recording and sharing a video of an incapacitated 17-year-old girl in April 2009. The woman, now 34, testified she had no memory of meeting Oren Alexander. Two women testified that they felt paralyzed before Oren and Alon Alexander assaulted them. The defense tried to undermine some of the accusers’ accounts, saying the sex was consensual and suggesting that the women were motivated by disappointment and were in it for financial gain. “And so, ask yourselves, are you hearing what these women actually remember from 10 to 15 years ago, or are you hearing stories that have been rehearsed and shaped by news articles and civil lawyers who stand to collect money at the end of this case?” Tal Alexander’s attorney, Deanna Paul, said during the trial. She said the women met up with the brothers “willingly” and “were free to come and go.” “The government has not proved it was a commercial sex act because there wasn’t one, and they have failed to meet their burden,” she said. In closing, Marc Agnifilo, Oren Alexander’s attorney, acknowledged that his client “built a lifestyle around pursuing women.” “They hurt a lot of people’s feelings while they were ascending professionally,” he said. “They said some things that were offensive and hurtful, and we got here because of that stuff, not because they are rapists or drugged women.” Assistant U.S. Attorney Elizabeth Espinosa said the defense was trying to confuse the jury. “There is no good reason why all these women would commit perjury and drag their friends and family into this. Why on Earth would they be here a decade later talking about their sex lives? They sat here in front of a group of strangers and detailed these horrific crimes,” she said. The three brothers showed no visible emotion as the verdicts were read. Their parents, as well as Alon Alexander's wife, were also present and did not visibly react or say anything. One of the jurors of said after the verdict, “It wasn’t easy.” The charges varied by brother. The three were charged with conspiracy to commit sex trafficking, sex trafficking and inducing a person to travel to engage in unlawful sexual activity. Tal Alexander was also charged with two additional counts of sex trafficking, an additional count of inducing a person to travel to engage in unlawful sexual activity and a count of sex trafficking of a minor. Alon Alexander was also charged along with Tal on the count of sex trafficking of a minor. Oren and Alon Alexander were also charged with one count each of aggravated sexual abuse by force or intoxicant and sexual abuse of a physically incapacitated person. Oren Alexander was also charged singly on a count of sexual exploitation of a minor. Agnifilo, the defense attorney who represents Oren Alexander, said they will appeal. "We believe in our clients’ innocence, and we will not stop fighting until we prevail, and we believe that we will one day prevail,” he said. The brothers' family called the verdict "deeply disappointing." "We believe there are substantial problems with the evidence and the way this case was presented. The legal process does not end here," the family said in a statement. "We will continue fighting every day until justice is done and the three brothers regain their freedom." The Alexander brothers face dozens of civil lawsuits. They have denied all allegations of misconduct. Oren and Alon Alexander also face criminal charges in Florida. On Thursday, a real estate broker in Beverly Hills, California, sued Oren Alexander, alleging he drugged and sexually assaulted her at a dinner in 2014. His civil attorney, Jason Goldman, said in a statement Thursday that the lawsuit was “salacious and demonstrably false” and that it was filed on the eve of jury deliberations as an “attempt to create headlines and taint the proceedings at a critical moment.” CORRECTION (Oct. 28, 2026, 10:56 p.m. E.T.): A previous version of this article incorrectly quoted a statement from Deanna Paul’s comments in court. She said, “And so, ask yourselves, are you hearing what these women actually remember from 10 to 15 years ago, or are you hearing stories that have been rehearsed and shaped by news articles and civil lawyers who stand to collect money at the end of this case?”

articles.title: Chimney sweep in Cornwall rescues owl trapped in stove
articles.summary: Rob Stead was attending a routine chimney clean in Polperro when he made the discovery.
articles.body:
A chimney sweep has managed to successfully rescue an owl that had got itself stuck in a chimney stove.

Rob Stead, 36, said he was completing a routine clean at a home in Polperro, Cornwall, last week when he noticed the bird peering through the glass of the stove in the living room.

He immediately alerted the owner of the property, who had been away for four weeks, and told him he would "do my best to free him".

Footage shows Stead using a towel to carefully collect the bird from inside the stove and, after checking it was OK, releasing it outside.

"I shone my torch in there and he started flapping," said Stead, who works in South East Cornwall.

"I got a towel wrapped around him, managed to take him out of the stove and I released him into the back garden.

"He didn't fly straight off but he flew into the corner of the garden there and he eventually took off."

The chimney sweep, who often finds nests and birds in the chimneys he cleans, said he was not an owl expert but figured he would use "a bit of common sense" to make the rescue.

He also noted that, had the bird had been looking "worse for wear", he would have called vets for help.

"He seemed quite happy flying off to the end of the garden," Stead said.

"I went over there and checked on him and he scuttled off. He seemed alright, so I left him to it."

Despite the homeowner being away for some time, Stead said he did not think the bird could have been trapped in the chimney for long.

"He seemed to regain his strength pretty fast as soon as I released him, so I think he was alright," he said.

He added: "I've rescued a robin before, I've rescued a jackdaw or two .. unfortunately you do get some dead birds come down too.

"There is nothing wrong with getting a bird guard and stopping the birds nesting in there."

On its website, the RSPB said it was "best to prevent birds nesting in chimneys" as it "reduces the risk of chimney fires, as well as avoiding injury to the birds and damage to their nest".

The charity added that any active nests must be left alone, but "if there are birds stuck in your chimney that aren't nesting, you can get them out".

If a bird was not injured, they could be released outside, it said.

articles.title: Twitchers raise cash to give Mundesley villagers tweet relief
articles.summary: Birdwatchers are giving "something back" after hundreds flocked to witness a rare sighting.
articles.body:
Birdwatchers are raising money to "give something back" to the village where hundreds of them flocked following a rare sighting.

Enthusiasts have been travelling to Mundesley in Norfolk since a northern nutcracker was spotted in a garden on Friday.

Wayne Glossop, who travelled from Rotherham in South Yorkshire to see the bird on Sunday, said a villager suggested raising money for the Mundesley Volunteer Inshore Lifeboat - and the idea prompted him to set up a crowdfunding page.

The 37-year-old said: "It is about giving something back to the community after hundreds of people turned up."

The bird had not been seen in Norfolk since 1968 and had not been widely spotted in the UK since 1991.

A spotting by one person was recorded in Caithness in Scotland in 2021, according to Bird Guides . Another was spotted by a few quick-moving twitchers in Kent in 1998.

The sighting saw about 150 people visit the village on Sunday alone, which led to bus services being disrupted because of people parking poorly on the road.

Glossop said: "When these rare birds turn up we all dash to go see it... and all of a sudden it was absolute carnage."

He said the local resident who gave the idea of fundraising had been collecting donations in person from birdwatchers, with more than £530 raised so far.

Meanwhile, a JustGiving page was set up by Glossop, with more than £1,200 raised for the lifeboat charity.

"Birdwatchers and twitchers are not always given the best rep, so to turn up on a quiet estate can be daunting, so we are giving back to the community," Glossop added.

The BBC has approached the lifeboat charity for comment.

Glossop said seeing the bird was "a milestone" after using the binoculars of his late friend.

"I inherited his binoculars and that was the 400th bird seen through them," he added.

articles.title: Beekeeping: More NI colonies survived winter last year, figures show
articles.summary: The annual honey bee husbandry survey by the Agri-Food and Biosciences Institute finds about one-in-four colonies were lost in 2025/26.
articles.body:
Fewer bee colonies were lost last winter in Northern Ireland, new figures show.

The annual honey bee husbandry survey by the Agri-Food and Biosciences Institute (AFBI) found about one-in-four colonies were lost in 2025/26, compared to a third in 2024/25.

About half (51%) the losses were linked to problems with the queen bee. Others were lost because bees were dead or the hive was empty. Natural hazards including storms, flood and theft accounted for 10%.

AFBI entomologist Joanna Kirbas said the survey was "essential" for monitoring bee health and detecting long-term trends.

Bees are an important species for human survival.

They pollinate a third of our food groups and roughly 80% of wildflowers.

But globally, populations are under pressure from climate change, habitat destruction and human activity including farming.

The annual survey has been running for 18 years, creating a snapshot of beekeeping practices and challenges in Northern Ireland.

Kirbas said the latest survey had the highest number of responses in five years, showing how invested beekeepers are in providing up-to-date information on the honey bee population.

"This survey is essential and allows AFBI to monitor honey bee health in Northern Ireland, track colony losses over winter, and examine the best methods of disease prevention."

More than a hundred beekeepers took part in this year's survey

They had a total of 570 living colonies before the winter of 2025/26

Of those, 130 were lost over winter - 24%

That is significantly lower than the 33% loss average reported in the winter of 2024/25, but similar to the 24% loss rate in 2023/24

Around 14% of colonies were lost in 2022/23 and 11% in 2021/22

The highest number was in 2012/13, when 43% of colonies was lost

A colony is lost when either the entire hive of honey bees has died or left, sometimes leaving behind a queen bee and some nurse bees.

Dr Archie Murchie, the head of AFBI's Plant Health and Integrated Pest Management branch, said building a picture of long-term trends played an important role in monitoring an important pollinator.

"Honey bee losses are largely driven by weather, which influences the bees themselves, their food sources and their susceptibility to infections," he said.

"While we don't yet have enough data to analyse long-term trends, changing weather patterns could be contributing to colony losses," Dr Murchie continued.

"It is vital that we continue to track colony losses as well as threats to honey bees."

The survey also covers disease management and prevention measures taken by beekeepers to control the Varroa mite.

It is a parasite that attacks and feeds on honey bees and can lead to the collapse and death of a colony.

But Dr Murchie said other diseases also pose a threat.

"There is a possibility that the Tropilaelaps mite, which attacks honey bee broods, could soon spread to Europe.

"The mite was found in Georgia in 2024 and has just been found in Turkey.

"The mites breed rapidly and can quickly overwhelm a hive."

articles.title: TSA finds sharp "mutant blades" in carry-on bag at Seattle airport
articles.summary: TSA officers at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport found sharp "mutant blades" in a carry-on bag that resembled something out of a comic book or horror fil...
articles.body:
Two TSA agents uncovered a sharp object that could have been plucked from the pages of a comic book or a horror film, while scanning luggage at the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. One agent said he'd never seen anything like it since joining TSA two years ago, while the agency described the offending item as "mutant blades."

The officers, identified as Douglas Linn and Dennis Oishi, spotted the blades while reviewing X-ray images at one of the airport's security checkpoints and proceeded to search the bag, TSA said .

What they found, the agency said, "resembled a mix between Wolverine-style claws and Freddy Krueger blades," referencing the fictional Marvel Universe character and the notorious villain from "A Nightmare on Elm Street." TSA said the dangerous discovery should serve as a reminder "that some accessories are better suited for movie screens than airplane cabins."

"Not a Marvel-ous idea in your carry-on bag," the agency wrote Tuesday in a post on X, which included photos of the spooky apparatus as well as a reminder to travelers: "Please pack all mutant blades in a checked bag."

Not a Marvel-ous idea in your carry-on bag. Adamantium-tally our SEA officers were amazed to see this image roll across their X-ray screen. Please pack all mutant blades in a checked bag. pic.twitter.com/NrjQIXinbz

Linn, the officer who initially flagged the carry-on bag containing the blades, recalled his surprise when they first popped up on the X-ray screen.

"I saw three blades and distinct claw-like features," he said in a statement. "I was amazed, and even more so when it came out of the bag. I had never seen anything like this during my two years at TSA."

The passenger, who said he'd forgotten the item was in his luggage, voluntarily abandoned the blades at the security checkpoint once Oishi, who'd searched the bag, removed them.

Ann Rhoades, the supervisory TSA officer, said in another statement that the blades were among "the most unusual items" she'd encountered in her seven years with the agency.

"My first thought was, 'Oh my gosh,' and my second thought was, 'Is this what I think it is?'" said Rhoades.

Air travelers are allowed to pack sharp objects, like box cutters, corkscrews, darts and knives in their checked baggage, as long as the items are "sheathed or securely wrapped to prevent injury to baggage handlers and inspectors," according to TSA's guidelines.

articles.title: UP MLC polls: In a close contest, BJP, SP finish with 6-5 scoreline; five key takeaways
articles.summary: UP MLC election results: BJP leads 6-5 over SP across 11 seats, winning 4 Teachers and 2 Graduates constituencies; SP wins 2 Teachers and 3 Graduates.
articles.body: BJP Retains 5 Of 6, Gains 1; SP Retains 3, Gains 2LUCKNOW: In a closely fought contest, the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Samajwadi Party ended the Legislative Council elections with a 6-5 scoreline for 11 seats in Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday. Results for all six Teachers’ constituencies and four of five Graduates’ constituencies had been declared by late Wednesday. The SP candidate had an unassailable lead in the Varanasi Graduates' constituency. The party also retained the Teachers' seat of the district.Of the six Teachers’ seats, BJP won four while the SP secured two. In the Graduates’ constituencies, BJP has won two seats and the SP three. BJP has retained five out of the six seats it had won in 2020, lost one and gained one seat. SP, on the other hand, retained its tally of three seats of 2020 and gained two new seats.Of the 11 seats, six — Lucknow Graduates', Lucknow Teachers', Meerut Graduates', Meerut Teachers', Agra Graduates' and Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers' — were held by BJP in 2020. The SP candidates won three seats: Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates', Varanasi Graduates and Varanasi Teachers.BJP retains Bareilly-Moradabad, Meerut Teachers’ constituenciesIndependent MLCs Dhruv Tripathi and Akash Agarwal won the remaining two seats — Teachers’ seats in Gorakhpur-Faizabad and Agra.However, Tripathi later joined the BJP, while Agarwal joined the SP just before the poll and entered the 2026 electoral contest as the party’s official candidate.This time, Tripathi won the closest contest of these polls in the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituency, defeating Independent candidate Rajiv Yadav by a narrow margin of 307 votes.Tripathi secured 16,790 votes, with the outcome decided after counting of second-preference votes. This was his fourth consecutive win. He had won as an independent on the previous three occasions.Following his victory, Tripathi acknowledged the tough competition posed by his rival and praised Rajiv Yadav for putting up a strong fight and winning the confidence of teachers.He said victory and defeat are part of the electoral process, but ultimately a win remains a win. In the Agra-Aligarh Teachers’ constituency, SP candidate Akash Agrawal defeated BJP’s Hari Kishore Tiwari by a margin of 4,263 votes.SP’s Kanti Singh avenged her defeat against BJP’s Avnish Kumar Singh, winning the seat by a margin of 17,225 votes. Kanti received 56,905 votes, while BJP’s Avnish secured 39,778 votes. Kanti had won the seat as an independent in 2014 but lost to Avnish in 2020.In the Varanasi Graduates’ constituency, SP’s Ashutosh Sinha took a decisive lead over BJP’s Kedar Nath Singh as the final preferential vote rounds concluded. After the 4th round of voting, Sinha secured 22,599 preferential votes against Singh’s 15,404 votes, opening up a commanding lead of 7,195 votes.In the Meerut Graduates’ constituency, BJP candidate Dinesh Kumar Goyal emerged victorious by approximately 13,000 votes against SP’s Paremendra Singh, while party colleague Manvendra Pratap Singh won the Agra Graduates’ seat against SP’s Shashank Yadav by a margin of8,856 votes. BJP had won both the seats in 2020.SP retained the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates’ constituency, where Maan Singh Yadav defeated BJP’sAshok Kumar Rathaur by a margin of27,663 votes.Among the Teachers’ constituencies, BJP candidate Umesh Dwivedi won the Lucknow seat defeating SP’s Sushil Kumar by4,808 votes,while SP candidate Lal Bihari Yadav retained Varanasi, overwhelming BJP’s Pramod Mishra by4,898 votes.Shrichand Sharma won the Meerut seat against SP’sNitin Tomar by13,241 votes, while Hari Singh Dhillon retained the Bareilly-Moradabad seat, defeating SP’s Danish Akhtar by17,676 votes.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: UN experts sound alarm at excessive use of force in French student protests
articles.summary: UN experts have condemned police crackdowns, warning they deter demonstrators from exercising their rights.
articles.body:
United Nations experts have expressed alarm at the “excessive use of force” by French authorities in dispersing the recent nationwide student protests.

“The scale of the arrests and detention, affecting several thousand people, mainly minors, appears disproportionate and deters demonstrators from exercising their freedoms of expression and peaceful assembly,” the four experts, mandated by the UN Human Rights Council, said in a statement on Wednesday.

They included Gina Romero, special rapporteur on the freedom of peaceful assembly, and Farida Shaheed, the UN expert on cultural rights.

“Although authorities launched several initiatives to facilitate dialogue and respond to students’ demands in October, the priority given to a primarily security-focused response to the protests has led to the root causes of the mobilisation being sidelined,” the statement said.

France has seen ongoing student protests since mid-September, sparked initially over conditions in high schools, where young people complained about the deteriorating buildings, overcrowded classrooms and teacher absences. Students have also joined nationwide demonstrations to express anger over the rising cost of living, which led to riots and looting on the sidelines.

The French government deployed 70,000 security forces and arrested 1,000 people during demonstrations on Saturday, which drew 410,000 protesters nationwide, France’s Interior Ministry said. A week earlier, public buildings were vandalised, hundreds of businesses were looted and 2,700 people were arrested, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez vowing to be “extremely vigilant, extremely firm” to quell future unrest.

“What we are seeing right now is a general outburst of resentment against [French President Emmanuel] Macron and his policies that have destroyed our rights, destroyed our living conditions,” Alice Cohen-Morzadec, a spokesperson for the Union Etudiante, told Al Jazeera .

Analysts say the French government has struggled to address students’ demands due to a severe fiscal crisis and planned budget cuts, which have led to a drop in the country’s education budget.

French authorities have been criticised for their approach to security during some of the protests, and in one case a teenager in the northern city of Lille lost a hand when a grenade exploded as school protesters clashed with police.

“The serious and, in some cases, irreversible injuries sustained by underage demonstrators during law enforcement operations are unacceptable and unjustifiable,” the UN rapporteurs said.

The statement added: “The experts recalled past discussions urging French authorities to undertake a comprehensive review of their policing strategies and practices in order to enable demonstrators to express their concerns and to facilitate a peaceful resolution of social conflicts.”

“The experts are in contact with French authorities on the issue,” the statement concluded.

articles.title: NHS Western Isles prescribing weight loss drugs at triple the rate of other health boards
articles.summary: A new report finds "significant variation" between Scotland's health boards prescribing new medicines.
articles.body:
Patients in the Western Isles are being prescribed drugs used for weight loss and diabetes at almost three times the rate of any other health board in Scotland.

A new report from the Association of the British Pharmaceutical Industry (ABPI) found "significant variation" between Scotland's health boards prescribing new medicines, including drugs for heart attacks and strokes.

The biggest variation was seen in access to GLP-1 medication, which is widely used to treat type 2 diabetes but was approved for weight management in 2023.

NHS Western Isles said it was seeing "significant clinical benefit".

The ABPI said there were limitations to the data, but better planning could help overcome inequalities in access.

The Scottish government said it would "carefully consider" the findings of the report.

It said its health board reforms were intended to "improve equity of access to services and reduce the unwarranted variation and bureaucratic barriers we currently have in place".

These reforms include plans to reduce the number of mainland health boards from 14 to two, which leading doctors have opposed.

This first-of-a-kind report from the body that represents pharmaceutical companies, compared access to several new medicines approved by the Scottish Medicines Consortium (SMC) as safe to use and value for money on the health service.

The analysis looked at NHS prescribing across all Scottish boards from September 2020 to August 2025.

The biggest variation for patients was in access to GLP-1medications which showed "substantial geographic variation".

The report sets out a three-month average quantity of the drug prescribed per head of population for each health board in Scotland, between June to August 2025.

NHS Western Isles prescribed the highest rate (1,086.54) followed by NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde (392.97). NHS Shetland had the lowest rate (100.31).

The report authors say there are limitations to the data with both boards at the end of the range serving small island populations, where a few prescriptions can make a big difference to prescribing rates.

It also highlighted that this data does not identify which were prescribed for diabetes and which for weight loss.

Earlier this month, BBC Scotland News revealed that fewer than half of Scotland's 14 territorial health boards were currently prescribing GLP-1s specifically for weight loss, and fewer than 800 Scots had received the jabs so far for this purpose.

The Royal College of Physicians described the lack of access to the "safe and cost-effective medicines" as "discriminatory against obese people", and argued the NHS could save millions in obesity-related illness.

According to freedom of information requests sent by BBC Scotland News, NHS Western Isles has 340 patients on medication for weight loss - the highest number of any board involved in the pilots.

NHS Western Isles is one of six health boards taking part in pilot programmes to improve access to weight loss medication.

The others are NHS Forth Valley, NHS Borders, NHS Lothian, NHS Lanarkshire, and the NHS State Hospital known as Carstairs.

NHS Western Isles said it established a "structured pathway" for access to GLP-1 medicines earlier than any other NHS board in Scotland.

It added: "Our prescribing rates reflect that early implementation, as well as local clinical need, rather than participation in a pilot scheme."

"These medicines are prescribed following clinical assessment and form part of a wider dietetic-led programme supporting long-term behaviour change and healthier lifestyles. Patients are reporting and we are seeing significant clinical benefit."

Call for better planning and transparency

The report also looked at access to certain medicines prescribed to patients with cardiovascular disease.

Cardiovascular disease, which includes conditions such as heart disease or stroke, is a leading cause of death and affects around 800,000 people in Scotland.

The study looked at prescribing data for non-statin low-density lipoprotein (LDL)-lowering medicines accepted by the SMC.

Prescribing rates differed eight-to-10-fold between the highest-prescribing (Highland) and lowest-prescribing (Forth Valley) boards.

Authors say health boards with closer links between specialists and GPs generally recorded higher prescribing.

The ABPI made seven recommendations, including better planning and co-operation alongside more transparency by health boards about decisions on what medicines to use locally, and how quickly accepted medicines are being introduced.

Victoria Jordan, ABPI executive director of patient access, said: "Scotland has a strong and respected system for assessing new medicines.

"But this report shows that the use of some accepted medicines can vary widely between NHS boards, and that differences in patient need do not fully explain this.

"While the data we have does not tell us everything, it does show we need to look more closely at this issue. When avoidable barriers slow things down, patients can wait longer than they should for medicines already judged effective and good value.

"We need to plan and work together across government, the NHS, clinicians, patients, academia and industry. That way, we can help make sure national SMC decisions have benefit to patients, wherever they live."

articles.title: Hidden danger in cockpit surfaces as 3 in 4 pilots report 'microsleep' episodes
articles.summary: Over 75% of pilots reported having "microsleep" episodes while flying, according to a major survey of 7,200 pilots. Experts weighed in on the topic amid flight safety concerns.
articles.body: A hidden problem is surfacing regarding certain pilots' behavior. More than three in four pilots reported having at least one "microsleep" while operating an aircraft in recent weeks, according to a report by aviation consultancy Baines Simmons based on responses from 7,200 pilots across 32 European countries. The findings were published by the European Cockpit Association (ECA), which represents over 44,000 pilots across Europe, according to a press release. HOW MUCH REST SHOULD FLIGHT ATTENDANTS GET? NEW PROPOSAL IGNITES FIGHT IN THE SKIES The concerns extend beyond brief episodes of sleep in the cockpit. Nearly 39% of pilots said they usually or always did not get enough rest to keep fatigue from building up, according to the report. The findings also raised questions about whether pilots feel comfortable reporting when they are too tired to fly. Only 37.2% said they typically report when they are too fatigued to fly, while 24.2% said they do not report it and fly anyway, according to the findings. "When pilots fear career consequences, fatigue goes unreported, and the risk returns to the cockpit," Capt. Coen George, an ECA board director, said in the press release. He warned that the reluctance to speak up could leave airlines unaware of how widespread fatigue is among their crews. In the United States, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) implemented stricter pilot rest and duty requirements in 2012 to address fatigue and improve safety, the agency said in a statement to Fox News Digital. Pilot fatigue can be particularly challenging when crews work overnight or travel across multiple time zones. Under the rules, pilots must receive at least 10 consecutive hours of rest before a flight duty period, including an opportunity for eight uninterrupted hours of sleep. Pilots who feel fatigued or unfit to fly must report it and be removed from duty by the airline, according to the FAA. Pilot fatigue can be particularly challenging when crews work overnight or travel across multiple time zones. Matthew "Whiz" Buckley, a former U.S. Navy F/A-18 Hornet fighter pilot who later flew for American Airlines and FedEx, previously told Fox News Digital that having scheduled time off does not necessarily mean a pilot gets enough sleep. "It's just unnatural to sleep during off-hours," Buckley said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES Pilots may arrive at a hotel early in the morning and then have to sleep during the day, while long-haul flights can further disrupt normal sleep patterns, Buckley said. "Where it really takes a toll on the body for pilots is east-west," he said. "When you're crossing multiple time zones, [that's] when your body can really get messed up." Buckley also emphasized that pilots ultimately have to assess whether they're rested enough to safely operate an aircraft. "At the end of the day ... you know who determines if a pilot is fit to fly? You," Buckley said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Having nearly "77% of respondents [in the new survey] say that they reported micro-sleeping or dozing off while at work is definitely an alarming number, and the industry does need to take note of this," Bobby Laurie, a Pennsylvania-based travel expert and former flight attendant, told Fox News Digital. "But it's not necessarily a warning sign that the flight that you've been on had a pilot or both pilots asleep." He said that while there are things the industry can do to "rectify this problem," travelers, too, should take note of a few things. "If you find yourself at the airport, and the departure board is saying you're delayed due to crew rest … you need to realize that the delay is posted for safety reasons. You might not have gotten to your destination in one piece if those crew members did not get the rest they needed," he said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Fox News Digital previously reported that rest requirements for flight attendants have faced scrutiny in the U.S. The FAA recently proposed a nationwide rule that would prevent state and local governments from setting separate meal and rest-break requirements for flight attendants and pilots. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Major flight attendant unions opposed the proposal, arguing that some crew members already work for hours without enough opportunities to eat, drink or use the restroom. articles.title: Why the US has become a political base for Brazil’s Bolsonaro allies
articles.summary: Three days after losing Brazil’s presidential election on Sunday, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami, joining other prominent allies of the Bolsonaro political movement who have sought refuge in the United States while facing legal troubles back home.
articles.body: Three days after losing Brazil’s presidential election on Sunday, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami, joining other prominent allies of the Bolsonaro political movement who have sought refuge in the United States while facing legal troubles back home. The defeated candidate reportedly crossed into Argentina with his wife and two daughters on Tuesday, then boarded a private plane that stopped in Ecuador before landing in South Florida. He left after a Supreme Court order, issued the day after the election, required him to surrender his passports and barred him from leaving Brazil. Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who has a long history of legal battles with the Bolsonaro family, issued the order citing a “concrete risk” that the senator would flee. On Friday, on the American conservative podcast Louder with Crowder, his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro had suggested that Flávio should leave Brazil if he lost to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, citing concerns about the investigations he could face once his Senate term ends. In a video posted Monday, Flávio Bolsonaro addressed his brother’s comments and promised to comply with the Supreme Court order, citing political persecution. His Senate term ends on January 31, 2027, leaving him out of elected office for the first time in 24 years. Flávio Bolsonaro is currently under investigation by the country’s highest court for alleged acts of corruption and money laundering. Upon arriving in the US, he released a three-page statement on Wednesday, declaring himself the “leader of Brazil,” despite losing Sunday’s runoff to Lula. He repeated unsubstantiated claims of electoral fraud, said it had not been his intention to leave the country and vowed to lead the Brazilian opposition from the United States. “I want to make it clear: I did not flee Brazil. I left for Brazil,” he wrote, describing himself as a victim of political persecution and thanking US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei for their support in his departure plans. A growing political base abroad In the United States, Flávio Bolsonaro joins a growing list of prominent figures in the Bolsonaro movement who have relocated there while facing legal trouble in Brazil. Eduardo, a former congressman, moved to the US in early 2025, saying he was the target of political persecution, and received permanent residency in July. Brazil’s Supreme Court has since sentenced him to four years and two months in prison for coercion, finding that he lobbied US officials to pressure the judges overseeing his father’s coup case. Moraes ordered his arrest this month. Former intelligence chief and congressman Alexandre Ramagem slipped out of Brazil through Guyana in September 2025, while the Supreme Court was still trying him for his role in the plot to overturn the 2022 election, and arrived in the US the day he was convicted. US immigration authorities detained him in Florida in April and released him two days later. His allies say he has applied for asylum. Conservative commentators Allan dos Santos and Paulo Figueiredo have also built platforms in the US while facing legal disputes in Brazil. Their cases differ, but together they suggest that the US has become more than a refuge for Bolsonaro allies. It is also a political base, with ideological allies, access to influential conservatives and a network of Brazilian supporters. “Exile is no longer isolation,” said Teresa Cristina Schneider Marques, a political scientist at PUCRS (Pontifical Catholic University of Rio Grande do Sul), who researches “Bolsonarismo” in the US. “With social media and the media, it has become a strategy for international and transnational projection.” Why the United States? The US is home to the largest Brazilian community abroad, with about two million people, according to estimates from Brazil’s Foreign Ministry. That community has historically leaned conservative. Brazilian voters in the US backed the right-wing candidate in the 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022 runoffs, according to Brazilian electoral data. This year they backed Flávio Bolsonaro, who won nearly 63% of their valid votes in Sunday’s runoff. The ties go beyond the ballot box. Connections between Brazilian conservative elites and American political figures deepened during the overlapping presidencies of Jair Bolsonaro — Flávio’s father — and Trump, whose movements share nationalist and socially conservative positions. After Jair Bolsonaro lost the 2022 election, thousands of his supporters stormed Brazil’s Congress, Supreme Court and presidential palace on January 8, 2023, in an attack that drew comparisons to the January 6, 2021, assault on the US Capitol. As legal pressure mounted, several prominent figures in his movement left for the United States. Since then, Marques said, the movement has worked to “domesticate the cause” on three fronts, persuading American society to adopt it as its own. The first is Washington, where allies have sought to influence US policy toward Brazil. The second is the media: Eduardo Bolsonaro and Figueiredo, among others, have used American podcasts, conservative outlets and social media to argue that Brazil’s judiciary is persecuting the right. The third is the Brazilian diaspora. “The diaspora plays an important role in spreading narratives, but also in translating them,” Marques said, “not just in English, but also adapting political messages so they resonate with American audiences.” Groups such as Yes Brasil in Florida and the Congresso Conservador Brasileiro in Massachusetts bring together supporters, Brazilian politicians and the immigrant community, and can act as intermediaries with American conservative circles. The result is a division of labor: prominent figures gain access to institutions and influential allies, while ordinary supporters spread the message among the Americans and Brazilians around them. The ultimate aim is to win American support and use it to pressure Brazilian institutions, a tactic scholars call the “boomerang effect” — in which political movements turn to international allies to influence decisions at home. A powerful ally in the White House Trump has repeatedly criticized Brazil’s judiciary over its treatment of Jair Bolsonaro, who was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison for the coup plot. That support has had concrete consequences. Last year, Trump imposed tariffs of up to 50% on Brazilian products, explicitly citing Jair Bolsonaro’s prosecution, and his administration sanctioned Brazilian judicial authorities. More recently, a Reuters investigation published ahead of Sunday’s runoff election, described efforts by two senior State Department officials to help the Bolsonaro family return to power, including measures intended to pressure Lula’s government. Trump has questioned the legitimacy of Brazil’s election, without providing evidence of fraud, pointing to a last-minute Supreme Court decision to extend voting by two hours, until 7 p.m., following reports of transportation problems. At a campaign rally in Texas on Tuesday, Trump also compared Brazil’s election to his longstanding allegations of electoral cheating by Democrats. Trump confirmed Wednesday that the US allowed Flávio Bolsonaro to enter the country. “Well, I’m not going to make a comment about that, but I know that we gave him a pass to come into the country, so we’ll see,” Trump told reporters before departing for Ohio. A Trump adviser had told CNN Tuesday that the president had approved allowing Flávio Bolsonaro into the United States, and US officials confirmed that the administration would issue visas to the senator and his family. It is unclear what visas they received or whether Flávio Bolsonaro will seek asylum. Permission to enter does not mean someone qualifies for asylum or is shielded from extradition. Marques argued that, for Trump, welcoming Bolsonaro allies has political value: their claims of persecution fit a narrative, shared across the global right, that portrays leftist governments as authoritarian. Granting asylum implicitly accuses another country of persecution, she noted. But Marques said that narrative is harder to sell about Brazil than about Venezuela or Cuba. “Lula ends up being a stone in the shoe of the global right,” she said. “Lula is respected abroad and submitted to the courts when he was jailed in 2018, which makes him hard to cast as an authoritarian.” His reelection has also energized left-wing leaders abroad, who see his comeback victory as a possible turning point after a series of right-wing electoral gains. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, for instance, celebrated Lula’s win as an inspiration ahead of Spain’s November 29 election, declaring: “What happened in Brazil will happen in Spain. The comeback of global progressivism has just begun.” Marques suggested that a current US welcome carries less weight than it once did. “It would be one thing for the Obama administration to receive someone from Brazil as persecuted. It’s another for the Donald Trump administration.” Nor is that protection necessarily permanent; a successive US administration might take a different view of the matter than Trump does. A risky strategy for Brazil’s right? Flávio received nearly 60 million votes in Sunday’s runoff, a sign of the right’s continued strength, and his sudden departure caught his own party off guard. Rogério Marinho, the senator who coordinated Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign, said Tuesday that party leaders had not been told of his travel plans. With Jair Bolsonaro serving his sentence under house arrest and Flávio and Eduardo abroad, some on the right are already looking to alternatives. “I think it’s a somewhat risky move, particularly the way Flávio did it,” Marques said. She sees exile as a deliberate political strategy, but unlike Eduardo, who presented his move as a political choice, Flávio Bolsonaro left immediately after a court order restricting his travel, feeding the perception that he fled to avoid prosecution. “The way it was done raised the costs of that strategy,” she said. The episode could give other conservative leaders an opening to distance themselves from the family, she said, though Brazil’s right has repeatedly struggled to build an identity independent of Jair Bolsonaro. “The big question now is how long the right will allow itself to remain tied to Bolsonarismo.” She also finds the persecution narrative hard to sustain at home, since the movement’s allies won a large share of Congress this month. Having Flávio and Eduardo in the US could strengthen the family’s international influence. But it also presents a striking paradox: the movement’s three most prominent figures are trying to shape Brazil’s political future while two face legal risks if they return to the country, and the third, Jair Bolsonaro, remains under house arrest. Marques expects the fight to play out on the international stage. Brazil could seek Flávio Bolsonaro’s extradition, she said, setting up a prolonged dispute over whether he is a fugitive or a dissident, along the lines of the Julian Assange or Edward Snowden cases. “Just as Bolsonarismo is trying to make this boomerang effect work with the right, the left will do the same,” she said. “Now the question is which way it will come back.”

articles.title: Israel poll results deadlocked amid historic showing by Arab parties
articles.summary: Anxious Israelis watched election results near completion Wednesday, as no clear winner emerged and weeks of negotiating could lie ahead for Prime
articles.body: Anxious Israelis watched election results near completion Wednesday, as no clear winner emerged and weeks of negotiating could lie ahead for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and an array of opposition parties trying to unseat him.Arab-led parties put up a historic showing, but it's not clear if the other opponents of Netanyahu's far-right govt would form a coalition with them for a majority of seats in parliament. Issues around the Palestinians and their descendants remain sensitive in Israel.In defiant comments - which showed his Likud party losing ground since 2022 election - Netanyahu dismissed the idea of partnering with Arab parties as treasonous. He won't work with the Arab-led parties, whose constituents make up 20% of Israel's population, and they have also ruled out any partnership.His top challenger, centrist former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has left the door open to partnering with Arab parties under certain conditions, including their recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and of Hamas as an extremist group.Emerging results indicated that neither Netanyahu's nor Eisenkot's coalition blocs would reach the 61 seats needed for a majority in 120-seat Knesset. Media projected 53 seats for Likud and allied parties, 48 for Yashar and allied parties and 19 for Arab-led parties. With 85% of votes counted, Bibi’s party has 20.8%, Eisenkot’s 16.1%Israeli voters choose parties, not individuals. With 85% of votes counted, Netanyahu’s Likud party has 20.8% and Eisenkot’s Yashar party has 16.1%. Arab-led parties had 14.9%. It’s not clear whether some of Eisenkot’s likely partners who have ruled out such an alliance will change their minds to force Netanyahu from office. Counting absentee ballots will last until Thursday evening. There are an estimated half-million of them from military personnel and diplomats. Nearly 78% of voters turned out, the highest since 1999.Voting reflected unease over Netanyahu’s alliance with the far-right and anger in a war-weary nation over military draft exemptions for the significant ultra-Orthodox Jewish population. The Likud party’s share of the vote declined from 23.4% in 2022. But results suggest opponents were unable to capitalise on the grief caused by the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023, attack to decisively push him from office. One far-right partner losing support was national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. For many Israelis, he represented the worst strain of Netanyahu’s govt, openly taunting Palestinian detainees.Vote-counting suggested Likud would remain the largest party and most likely to be tapped to form a govt by Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog. The president, however, isn’t required to task the leader of the party holding the most seats. “We must do everything we can, to avoid another round of elections,” Herzog said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Convicted murderer got over 5-hour head start after prison escape before local police were notified: official
articles.summary: Jacob Allen Morley had at least a five-hour head start before Tiptonville police were notified he escaped the Northwest Correctional Complex.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: The convicted murderer who escaped from a Tennessee prison had at least a five-hour head start before local police were notified he was missing, the local police chief told Fox News Digital. Jacob Allen Morley broke out of the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, Sunday, although authorities have not disclosed the exact time of his escape. Staff at the prison noticed Morley was unaccounted for at around 11:30 p.m., and a review of surveillance footage subsequently revealed him crossing through the prison's perimeter fence. According to Tennessee Highway Patrol dispatch audio, Morley was last seen at the prison around 4 p.m. Sunday. Surveillance footage recorded Morley taking a pickup truck from the 400 block of Keystone Drive, a location roughly 2 miles south of the prison, at around 1 a.m. Monday, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said. The truck was found abandoned by law enforcement officials early Tuesday morning in Marion, Illinois, but Morley wasn't located. TENNESSEE INMATE CONVICTED OF MURDER ESCAPES FROM PRISON, STEALS PICKUP TRUCK, MANHUNT UNDERWAY: OFFICIALS In a statement to Fox News Digital, Tiptonville Police Department Chief Joe England said his department wasn't notified about a potentially missing inmate until 4:40 a.m. on Monday, over 5 hours after prison staff first realized Morley was unaccounted for. Officers responded to the prison and worked with staff to assess the situation. At 5:14 a.m., England said, officers alerted the rest of the department that the inmate's escape had been confirmed. At 6:20 a.m., prison officials formally notified Lake County Central Dispatch, which handles 911 calls and coordinates law enforcement services, that an inmate escape had been confirmed. The notification set off a broader search for Morley in the area surrounding the prison. ESCAPED TENNESSEE KILLER'S ABANDONED TRUCK OFFERS CLUES TO WHAT HE MAY DO NEXT: RETIRED FBI AGENT "The Tiptonville Police Department immediately coordinated with the Tennessee Department of Correction and the Lake County Sheriff's Office to conduct a search of the surrounding area," England said. "The Tennessee Highway Patrol, Tennessee Bureau of Investigation and numerous other state, local and federal law enforcement agencies also participated in the search efforts." While Morley stole the pickup truck at around 1 a.m. Monday, England said his department wasn't made aware of a potentially missing truck until 2:15 p.m. Monday, which was confirmed missing at 2:30 p.m. He noted that the pickup truck wasn't stolen within city limits. Timeline of Events: Sunday, Oct. 25 Monday, Oct. 26 Tuesday, Oct. 27 In a statement to Fox News Digital, a Tennessee Bureau of Investigation spokesperson said the agency was notified of the prison escape on Monday morning but didn't elaborate on an exact time. The Lake County Sheriff's Office didn't respond to Fox News Digital when asked when the agency was first alerted of the prison escape. The Tennessee Department of Correction didn't respond to multiple requests for comment to Fox News Digital. Former federal prison Warden Cameron Lindsay told Fox News Digital the delay in notifying police of an inmate escaping prison is "100% unacceptable." "Part of any correctional facility's basic tenets of operations should include emergency plans. And one of those plans that you have for an emergency is an escape. And part of your escape plans entails notifying law enforcement, local law enforcement, state law enforcement, U.S. Marshals Service and everybody in the community. You need to get that word out immediately. So, for them to have that kind of delay raises a huge red flag," Lindsay said. "And it begs the question, why, why did they delay? Because it is 100% unacceptable in the profession of corrections." Lindsay said local law enforcement should have immediately been contacted once prison staff realized the inmate was unaccounted for. Retired FBI Special Agent Jonathan Gilliam told Fox News Digital the community should have been notified much sooner. "That community should put out an emergency text to everyone to make sure none of their family members are missing as he could have killed or kidnapped someone after ditching the truck," Gilliam said. TBI said Wednesday afternoon that the reward in the search for Morley is now $15,000 — $7,500 from the governor’s office, $5,000 from the U.S. Marshals and $2,500 from TBI. Morley is described as 5 feet, 11 inches tall, and 240 pounds, with brown hair and green eyes. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said he should be "considered dangerous," adding Morley is now on the state's most wanted list. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X In addition to the first-degree murder conviction, he was also found guilty of burglary, vandalism, tampering with evidence and evading arrest. Morley was serving a life sentence for the 2022 murder of Cody Birchfield. Birchfield disappeared in early February 2022 after he was last seen in Elizabethton, Tennessee. According to WJHL, investigators from the Carter County Sheriff's Office saw indications that a "violent crime" had occurred inside his house. After the arrest, Birchfield's body was found underneath Morley's home. Pike survived the Sept. 30 execution attempt after the state administered two doses of pentobarbital, and she was transported to a hospital. Gov. Bill Lee then suspended Tennessee's remaining scheduled execution for the year and directed an independent review to examine what had gone wrong. articles.title: A man who committed murder at 17 was sentenced after turning 18 to a minimum of 15 years in prison; the UK Supreme Court ruled he could not seek a special review of that term
articles.summary: A man who committed murder at the age of 17 but was sentenced after turning 18 cannot seek a special review of his minimum prison term, the UK Supreme
articles.body: A man who committed murder at the age of 17 but was sentenced after turning 18 cannot seek a special review of his minimum prison term, the UK Supreme Court has ruled. The unanimous decision concerns Jesse Quaye, who received a minimum term of 15 years for murder and challenged legislation preventing him from applying for a reduction based on his progress in custody. In its judgment on 22 September 2026, the court upheld the legal restrictions, finding that they did not breach his human rights or amount to unlawful discrimination.Why the UK Supreme Court rejected the request to review his 15-year prison termThe case, R (on the application of Quaye) v Secretary of State for Justice, examined whether people who commit murder before turning 18 should retain the right to seek a review of their minimum prison term if they are sentenced after reaching adulthood.According to the Supreme Court's official case summary, Quaye committed the offences on 10 May 2014, when he was 17 years and 9 months old. He and a friend went uninvited to a party in Norfolk, where they stabbed and killed Connor Barrett. Quaye was also convicted of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and possessing a knife.He was convicted on 20 November 2014, aged 18 years and three months. On 16 January 2015, he was sentenced to detention at His Majesty's pleasure, with a minimum term of 15 years. He was then 18 years and five months old.The court's press summary explains that detention at His Majesty's pleasure is an indeterminate sentence imposed on people who commit murder while under 18. The sentencing judge sets a minimum period that must be served before the offender can apply to the Parole Board for release on licence.The sentence does not guarantee release after the minimum term. The Parole Board must assess whether continued detention is necessary to protect the public.How did the rules on minimum-term reviews changeFor years, the government operated a policy allowing people serving detention-at-His-Majesty's-pleasure sentences to apply for a review after completing half their minimum term. The review could lead to a reduction if the prisoner had made exceptional progress in custody.The Supreme Court judgment explains that the policy was based on the government's power to grant clemency. It did not provide an automatic reduction in the sentence, but an opportunity for eligible prisoners to demonstrate that their progress justified reconsideration.The position changed on 18 February 2021, when the Secretary of State introduced a revised policy excluding offenders who were already 18 or older when sentenced. This meant that Quaye could no longer apply for a review when he reached the halfway point of his minimum term on 15 March 2022.Parliament subsequently placed the restriction on a statutory footing through section 128 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. The provision amended the Crime (Sentences) Act 1997 by introducing sections 27A and 27B, which came into force on 28 June 2022.Under the new rules, eligibility depends on the offender's age when the sentence is imposed. Those sentenced before their 18th birthday can apply for a minimum-term review, while those sentenced at 18 or older cannot.Why did Quaye challenge the legislationQuaye sought a judicial review, arguing that the restrictions were incompatible with the European Convention on Human Rights. His challenge focused on the right to liberty and security, protection against discrimination and the prohibition on imposing a heavier penalty retrospectively.The Divisional Court initially ruled in his favour, declaring the legislation incompatible with the right to liberty and the prohibition on discrimination when read together with that right. It considered that removing the possibility of a review could create a risk of arbitrary detention and that the difference in treatment based on the date of sentencing lacked adequate justification.However, the Secretary of State successfully appealed. The Court of Appeal overturned the declarations of incompatibility, prompting Quaye to take his case to the Supreme Court.According to the Supreme Court's case records, the appeal was heard on 22 and 23 June 2026. The five justices considering the case were Lord Sales, Lord Briggs, Lord Hamblen, Lord Stephens and Lady Simler.Court found the restrictions compatible with human rightsIn its judgment, delivered by Lord Stephens and Lady Simler with the agreement of the other justices, the Supreme Court unanimously dismissed the appeal.On the right to liberty, the court found that the sentence had been imposed lawfully and that there was no general requirement for every indeterminate sentence imposed on a child to include periodic reviews of its minimum term.The judges explained that legislation had fundamentally changed the nature of detention at His Majesty's pleasure. The sentencing court now fixes the minimum term, while the Parole Board assesses the offender's suitability for release after that period. The Secretary of State no longer has a general power to reconsider the minimum term through the former clemency policy.The court decided that removing the opportunity to seek a reduction did not make Quaye's continued detention arbitrary or unlawful.It also rejected his discrimination argument. Although the law treats offenders differently according to their age at sentencing, the court found that Parliament had a legitimate reason for drawing this distinction. The restrictions were intended, in part, to reduce the distress experienced by victims' families when offenders apply for reviews.Families may be contacted whenever an offender seeks a review and given the opportunity to submit a new victim personal statement.The ruling leaves the original minimum-term framework unchangedThe Supreme Court also rejected Quaye's argument under Article 7 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which protects against the retrospective imposition of a heavier penalty.The judges distinguished between changing the punishment itself and changing how that punishment is administered. They found that the 2022 legislation did not alter Quaye's original sentence of detention with a minimum term of 15 years. Instead, it removed an opportunity to seek a reduction during the enforcement of that sentence.The court held that the change did not amount to the retrospective imposition of a heavier penalty.You use AI every day. articles.title: BOBBY BURACK: Justin Tucker signing exposes sports media’s selective outrage over NFL misconduct
articles.summary: Justin Tucker's practice squad signing sparked fierce criticism, but Andy Reid and the Chiefs face questions about the NFL's personal conduct policy.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs signed kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad Wednesday, drawing fierce criticism from the sports media. Head coach Andy Reid faced five straight minutes of questions about Tucker during his news conference. "He’s done his suspension. Took care of his business there. I’ll leave it at that," Reid said. The NFL suspended Tucker for 10 games in 2025 for violating its personal conduct policy after 16 female massage therapists accused him of sexual misconduct in the Baltimore area between 2012 and 2016. Tucker vehemently denies the allegations, including in a statement to OutKick at the time of the claims. The usual suspects criticized the move. "It only takes one ounce of desperation from one franchise to welcome back into the league somebody who was a pariah," Dan Le Batard said. ESPN analyst Mina Kimes responded by posting a screenshot of the allegations against Tucker. Several Kansas City media members also expressed frustration with the signing. But a proper response to the signing is not as binary as one on social media. articles.title: Cidade onde Nikolas gravou vídeo é a mais 'bolsonarista' da Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Luís Eduardo Magalhães esteve no topo do ranking das que mais votaram em pai e filho no estado, nas últimas eleições.
articles.summary: Luís Eduardo Magalhães esteve no topo do ranking das que mais votaram em pai e filho no estado, nas últimas eleições.
articles.body:
Cidade onde Nikolas gravou vídeo é a mais 'bolsonarista' da Bahia — Foto: Redes Sociais/ACICLEM

A cidade de Luís Eduardo Magalhães , onde o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira ( PL -MG) gravou o polêmico vídeo sobre o Nordeste , é a mais "bolsonarista do estado".

É o que apontam registros das últimas eleições em que a família concorreu à Presidência. Nas três ocasiões, o município do oeste baiano esteve no topo do ranking das cidades onde eles venceram.

Em 2018, quando Jair Bolsonaro (então PSL ) concorreu contra Fernando Haddad (PT) no segundo turno, a vitória no município foi por 58,8%.

No segundo turno de 2022, na disputa com Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), Jair Bolsonaro conquistou 58,61% dos votos na cidade — um resultado expressivo na Bahia, que deu maioria dos votos a Lula. De modo geral, o petista venceu o pleito no país e retornou à Presidência.

Já em 2026, o segundo turno foi encerrado com 61,6% dos votos para Flávio Bolsonaro e 38,4% para Lula, considerando apenas a votação em Luís Eduardo Magalhães. Mais uma vez, Lula teve ampla vantagem na Bahia e conquistou maioria no Brasil, sendo reeleito.

Além de Luís Eduardo Magalhães, apenas Buerarema , no sul da Bahia, surge na relação em todas as últimas eleições. Confira abaixo:

Eleições de 2018 : Jair venceu em Luís Eduardo Magalhães, Buerarema, Teixeira de Freitas e Itapetinga.

Eleições de 2022 : Jair venceu em Luís Eduardo Magalhães e Buerarema.

Eleições de 2026 : Flávio venceu em Luís Eduardo Magalhães, Buerarema, Itamaraju e Teixeira de Freitas.

Luís Eduardo Magalhães tem grande influência da região Sul do Brasil e detém, atualmente, o 6º maior Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) do estado.

Emancipado há apenas 26 anos, o município era um distrito de Barreiras, antes de ganhar o posto de cidade, em março de 2000. Mas o pontapé para o crescimento começou ainda na década de 1970 , com a imigração de famílias, sobretudo do Rio Grande do Sul, atraídas por terras baratas.

Na época, conforme o histórico, cada hectare (o que corresponde a 10 mil m²) era vendido por algo em torno de R$ 20. Atualmente, esse valor pode passar de R$ 30 mil, dependendo da produtividade da terra.

E foi exatamente o alto nível de produtividade que garantiu a expansão do cultivo de grãos e dos negócios na cidade. São construtoras, restaurantes, lojas e grandes revendedoras de equipamentos agrícolas.

A busca por esse tipo de negócio atrai milhares de pessoas, todos os anos, para o Bahia Farm Show (BFS) , segundo maior evento do agronegócio brasileiro e o mais importante do Norte/Nordeste, que acontece no município.

A área atual é de mais de 4 mil km², com uma população superior a 107 mil pessoas, conforme o último senso do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

Bahia Farm Show 2024, em Luís Eduardo Magalhães — Foto: Divulgação/Bahia Farm Show

Em 2023, data do último levantamento do IBGE sobre o tema, o PIB per capita de Luís Eduardo Magalhães era de R$ 107.118,26.

Na comparação com outros municípios do estado, a cidade fica atrás apenas de Salvador, Camaçari, São Francisco do Conde, Feira de Santana e Vitória da Conquista, na ordem.

Já entre os municípios de todo o país, a cidade ocupa a 231ª posição de 5570.

Apesar da grande diferença da porcentagem de votos, o presidente Lula (PT) ampliou sua votação no segundo turno no município. Na primeira rodada de votação, ele recebeu 20.173 votos na cidade. Na segunda, chegou a 24.739 — um crescimento de 22,6%.

Já Flávio, o candidato mais votado na cidade, passou de 38.496 votos no primeiro turno para 39.688 no segundo, um aumento de 3,1%. Com isso, a vantagem de Flávio sobre Lula caiu de 18.323 para 14.949 votos entre turnos.

Lula (PT) foi reeleito presidente do Brasil no domingo (25) com 51,7% dos votos contra 48,2% de votos de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em todo o país. O petista venceu em 413 dos 417 municípios baianos.

articles.title: Projetos valorizam áreas gourmet cada vez mais conectadas à casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Conexões com cozinha, varanda e jardim transformam o espaço de receber em uma extensão dos ambientes internos.
articles.summary: Conexões com cozinha, varanda e jardim transformam o espaço de receber em uma extensão dos ambientes internos.
articles.body:
A área gourmet passou a ocupar uma posição diferente na arquitetura residencial. Em muitos projetos, ela deixou de aparecer como um espaço isolado, reservado apenas para ocasiões especiais, e passou a estabelecer uma relação mais direta com a cozinha, a varanda, o jardim e a piscina. Essa proximidade encurta percursos e faz com que o local também participe da rotina da casa.

Essa mudança interfere nas decisões tomadas desde o início. Antes de definir revestimentos e acabamentos, é importante entender como a área será utilizada. Uma família que prepara refeições com frequência apresenta necessidades diferentes de quem concentra o uso nos fins de semana. Número de pessoas, circulação, equipamentos previstos e conexão com outros cômodos ajudam a determinar dimensões da bancada, áreas de apoio e distribuição do mobiliário.

O porcelanato da Eliane contribui para criar continuidade visual na área gourmet integrada, aproximando bancada, mobiliário, madeira e elementos naturais em uma mesma composição — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Mais do que um elemento visual, a bancada pode determinar boa parte do funcionamento da área gourmet. É nela que podem estar cuba, torneira, área de preparo e superfícies de apoio. Por isso, altura, profundidade e extensão precisam considerar tanto os equipamentos escolhidos quanto o espaço necessário para circulação durante o uso.

Os porcelanatos de grandes formatos ampliaram as possibilidades para esse tipo de aplicação. Quando possuem indicação adequada do fabricante, podem revestir bancadas e outros volumes com menor interferência de juntas, permitindo que o desenho da superfície apareça em áreas maiores.

Antes da execução, porém, é necessário prever recortes para cuba, encontros, quinas e demais particularidades da instalação. Essas definições precisam ser alinhadas com o profissional responsável para que estética e execução caminhem juntas.

A circulação também merece atenção. Quando a cozinha e área gourmet ficam próximas, o deslocamento durante o preparo das refeições tende a ser menor. Já na conexão com piscina e jardim, entram outras condições, como maior fluxo de pessoas, contato com água e exposição de determinadas superfícies ao clima.

A conexão com piscina, jardim e áreas internas interfere tanto na circulação quanto na definição dos revestimentos e acabamentos utilizados na área gourmet — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Essas diferenças de uso orientam a especificação dos materiais. Uma parede protegida junto à bancada enfrenta condições distintas de um piso exposto à chuva ou localizado próximo à piscina. Mesmo dentro da mesma área, portanto, diferentes superfícies podem exigir características técnicas específicas.

Por isso, a indicação de aplicação informada pelo fabricante precisa ser considerada junto com cor, textura e desenho. A continuidade visual pode ser mantida sem que todos os pontos recebam exatamente o mesmo acabamento.

Paredes também ajudam a organizar a composição

O revestimento vertical pode marcar a região da bancada, criar um fundo para a churrasqueira ou estabelecer uma transição com a cozinha. Nesse caso, textura, formato, manutenção e relação com os demais materiais entram na decisão junto com a tonalidade.

O porcelanato Legno Dorato, da Biancogres, leva a aparência da madeira para a parede e ajuda a aquecer visualmente a área gourmet, criando contraste com a bancada escura e reforçando a conexão com os elementos naturais ao redor — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

A composição tende a funcionar melhor quando cada superfície assume um papel. Se a bancada apresenta desenho mais marcante, a parede pode ter uma presença discreta. Quando o revestimento vertical ganha protagonismo, pisos, marcenaria e outros acabamentos podem trabalhar com uma linguagem mais neutra.

Essa diferença de intensidade permite que pedra, madeira, metais e revestimentos convivam sem disputar atenção.

Na hora de definir os materiais, levar planta e medidas para a Vilarejo ajuda a analisar as alternativas de acordo com a configuração real do espaço. Bancada, revestimentos e acabamentos podem ser comparados considerando aplicação, proporção e relação com as áreas próximas, em vez de serem avaliados isoladamente.

Uma área gourmet integrada começa, portanto, antes da escolha dos acabamentos. É a maneira como preparo, circulação e convivência se relacionam com cozinha, jardim e piscina que orienta sua organização. Quando essas necessidades entram no planejamento desde o início, o espaço deixa de ser um anexo da residência e passa a fazer parte naturalmente da arquitetura e da rotina.

articles.title: Áreas de vegetação nativa ficaram menores e mais isoladas no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Número de fragmentos cresceu 45% desde 1986, segundo o MapBiomas. Ao mesmo tempo, a área média dessas porções de vegetação caiu 43%.
articles.summary: Brasil tinha 2,35 milhões de fragmentos em 1986 e chegou a 3,41 milhões em 2024. Área média dessas porções de vegetação caiu 43% no período.
articles.body:
Área de desmatamento da Mata Atlântica no Paraná, em sobrevoo da SOS Mata Atlântica em março de 2023. — Foto: Zig Koch/SOS Mata Altântica/Mata Atlântica

As áreas de vegetação nativa do Brasil ficaram menores e mais isoladas nas últimas décadas. Em 2024, o país tinha 3,41 milhões de fragmentos , número 45% maior do que o registrado em 1986, segundo novos dados do MapBiomas.

No mesmo período, a área média de cada fragmento caiu de 287 para 163 hectares , uma redução de 43%.

Na prática, isso significa que, além da perda de vegetação nativa, parte do que restou ficou dividida em porções menores e com menos conexão entre si.

Fragmentos são áreas de vegetação nativa separadas por locais onde a cobertura original foi retirada para dar espaço, por exemplo, a pastagens , lavouras ou cidades .

Esse processo pode dificultar o deslocamento e a reprodução de animais e plantas, reduzir a troca genética entre populações e aumentar a exposição da vegetação ao fogo e aos chamados efeitos de borda.

Minas Gerais, Bahia, Goiás, São Paulo e Paraná concentram juntos 49% de todos os fragmentos de vegetação nativa do país.

Isso não significa, porém, que esses estados tenham as maiores áreas preservadas. Segundo o MapBiomas, a concentração revela justamente uma paisagem onde a vegetação está mais dividida .

Na região Norte, por outro lado, ainda estão as maiores áreas contínuas de vegetação nativa. No Amazonas, cada fragmento tem, em média, cerca de 4 mil hectares.

Em 46% dos municípios brasileiros, por outro lado, a área média dos fragmentos é inferior a 25 hectares, principalmente nas regiões Sul e Sudeste.

São João de Meriti, no Rio de Janeiro, aparece com a menor média do país: apenas 1,9 hectare por fragmento.

Entre os biomas, a Mata Atlântica concentra o maior número de fragmentos, com 1,38 milhão, seguida pelo Cerrado, com 957 mil .

A Amazônia também apresentou avanço expressivo da fragmentação. Desde 1986, o número de fragmentos no bioma cresceu 260%, de 144 mil para 519 mil. Ao mesmo tempo, a área média caiu 76%, de 2,7 mil para 662 hectares.

O levantamento também mostra que entre 10% e 24% da vegetação nativa brasileira estava exposta, em 2024, a pelo menos um fator de degradação, como fogo, isolamento, bordas, corte seletivo ou alterações no dossel.

A Mata Atlântica é o bioma proporcionalmente mais exposto a esses fatores. Dependendo do critério adotado, entre 33% e 70% de sua vegetação nativa estava sob algum tipo de pressão.

Em área absoluta, o Cerrado tem os maiores valores, entre 17,7 milhões e 42,1 milhões de hectares expostos à degradação.

Segundo o MapBiomas, os dados podem ajudar a orientar ações de restauração e de reconexão entre áreas de vegetação nativa.

articles.title: Praticidade da cozinha profissional inspira novos projetos residenciais com soluções DAX | G1
articles.standfirst: Cubas amplas, metais versáteis e áreas de apoio bem planejadas ajudam a tornar o preparo mais eficiente no dia a dia.
articles.summary: Cubas amplas, metais versáteis e áreas de apoio bem planejadas ajudam a tornar o preparo mais eficiente no dia a dia.
articles.body:
Nas cozinhas profissionais, cada movimento é pensado para reduzir deslocamentos e facilitar tarefas que se repetem ao longo do dia. Essa lógica também começa a aparecer nas residências, não pela estética industrial, mas pela organização das áreas de trabalho. Cubas maiores, metais com maior alcance e bancadas planejadas para lavagem, preparo e apoio são exemplos de recursos que tornam o uso mais prático.

O ponto de partida está na sequência das tarefas. Retirar alimentos, higienizar, preparar, cozinhar e limpar formam um fluxo. Quando cuba, torneira, bancada e equipamentos são distribuídos considerando essa ordem, os deslocamentos diminuem e cada função encontra um lugar mais definido.

A Cuba Baikal 76x46, da DAX, oferece uma área ampla para lavagem e facilita o manuseio de panelas, assadeiras e utensílios de maior volume — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

A Baikal, da DAX , é uma cuba de embutir em aço inox, com 76 cm de largura, 46 cm de profundidade e 22 cm de altura , acabamento fosco e válvula de 4,5 polegadas. O formato oferece mais espaço para atividades que podem se tornar limitadas em cubas menores.

As cubas, produzidas em aço inox 304, garantem mais qualidade e acabamento para as cozinhas e áreas gourmet.

O alcance da água também interfere no uso

Em uma área de lavagem mais ampla, a mobilidade do metal pode fazer diferença. Bicas móveis e flexíveis permitem levar o jato a diferentes pontos da cuba, aproximando a água dos alimentos, utensílios ou recipientes que estão sendo higienizados.

O Monocomando Bayoz, da DAX, possui bica móvel com giro de 360 graus, ampliando o alcance da água dentro da cuba e facilitando diferentes tarefas — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

No Monocomando Bayoz, da DAX , a bica possui giro de 360 graus e uma única alavanca permite controlar vazão e temperatura. O modelo conta ainda com cartucho cerâmico, arejador articulado e instalação de mesa. Segundo a ficha técnica oficial, funciona entre 5 e 40 m.c.a., suporta água a até 70 °C e é composto por ligas de cobre, elastômeros e plástico de engenharia. A garantia é de 10 anos, com prazo de um ano para peças móveis, conforme as condições da marca.

Esses recursos, porém, funcionam melhor quando são considerados ainda no planejamento da bancada. Uma cuba maior precisa de área de apoio compatível ao redor, enquanto uma bica com maior mobilidade deve ser instalada em uma posição que permita aproveitar seu alcance.

Também vale prever locais para escorrer louças, apoiar alimentos e organizar acessórios. Em vez de concentrar todas as funções em um único ponto, dividir a bancada de acordo com as tarefas ajuda a deixar a sequência de preparo mais organizada.

A inspiração profissional não significa transformar a cozinha residencial em um ambiente comercial. O principal aprendizado está em pensar o espaço a partir do que acontece nele. Quando lavagem, preparo e apoio são planejados de acordo com a rotina, os equipamentos passam a contribuir de maneira mais efetiva para o uso diário.
